title: Fuel can separation during evacuation
summary: A safe boundary for carrying or storing small fuel containers during evacuation, generator support, farm movement, or vehicle disruption without putting fumes near people.
content: This card improves fuel can separation during evacuation by making the action small, visible, and reversible. It helps a tired group avoid hidden assumptions while preserving emergency-service priority. Core sequence: 1) Keep fuel outside living, sleeping, cooking, and passenger areas whenever possible. 2) Label the fuel type and owner before containers are moved or shared. 3) Separate fuel from food, medicines, children, pets, ignition sources, and hot surfaces. 4) Stop transport if odor, leakage, swelling, heat, or confusion over contents appears. Stop point: Do not use fuel can separation during evacuation to bypass emergency responders, utility professionals, medical advice, or evacuation instructions.
